title: Isolation of Endothelial Cells from Umbilical Vessels
author: Thomas Mudersbach
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ybdfsi6
materials: Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) (H6648-500ml, Sigma-Aldrich) Enzymatic digestion with Dispase II (29585300, Roche) (2.4 U/ml) in Ham's F12 Ham's F12 with 10% fetal calf serum (FCS), penicillin (50 U/ml) and streptomycin (50 µg/ml) for centrifugation Endothelial cell culture medium: MCDB131 (10372-019, Gibco) containing 10% FCS, L-glutamine (10mM), penicillin (50 U/ml), streptomycin (50 µg/ml), epidermal growth factor (0.1 ng/ml), basic fibroblast growth factor (1 ng/ml) and endothelial growth supplement with Heparin (0.4%)

Hank's Balanced Salt Solution (HBSS) (H6648-500ml, Sigma-Aldrich) Enzymatic digestion with Dispase II (29585300, Roche) (2.4 U/ml) in Ham's F12 Ham's F12 with 10% fetal calf serum (FCS), penicillin (50 U/ml) and streptomycin (50 µg/ml) for centrifugation Endothelial cell culture medium: MCDB131 (10372-019, Gibco) containing 10% FCS, L-glutamine (10mM), penicillin (50 U/ml), streptomycin (50 µg/ml), epidermal growth factor (0.1 ng/ml), basic fibroblast growth factor (1 ng/ml) and endothelial growth supplement with Heparin (0.4%)

steps.title: Prepare and cannulate vessel ends
steps.instruction: Cut the umbilical cord about 1 cm from one end to expose the arteries and vein, then cannulate the chosen vessel (vein or artery) with a button cannula attached to a three‑way stopcock and secure it with a cable connector. Rinse the cannulated segment with HBSS until the wash is clear and no blood is observed. Repeat this entire procedure on the opposite end of the cord.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion with Dispase II
steps.instruction: Fill the now‑cannulated vessel with Dispase II solution and incubate the cord for 50 minutes at 37 °C.

steps.title: Replace enzyme and massage cord
steps.instruction: Discard the Dispase II solution, add Ham's F12 medium containing 10 % fetal calf serum (FCS), and gently massage the cord to loosen the endothelial cells into the medium.

steps.title: Collect cells and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Collect the medium in a suitable centrifuge tube, spin at 100 × g for 5 minutes, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the cell pellet in endothelial cell culture medium.

steps.title: Prepare fibronectin‑coated dish
steps.instruction: Coat a cell‑culture dish with fibronectin 30–60 minutes before use.

steps.title: Seed cells and incubate
steps.instruction: Distribute the resuspended endothelial cells onto the fibronectin‑coated dish and place the dish in a cell incubator set to 37 °C with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Wash cells after 4 hours
steps.instruction: Four hours after seeding, wash the cells gently with fresh cell‑culture medium.

steps.title: Grow to confluence (48‑96 h)
steps.instruction: Maintain the cultures; between 48 and 96 hours after isolation the endothelial cells should form a confluent monolayer.
